Baby Milestones Month by Month (0–12 Months)

Güncellendi: July 1, 2026

Bu yazı, çevirisi hazırlanana kadar İngilizce gösterilir.

The first year is a whirlwind of change: a newborn who mostly sleeps becomes a babbling, cruising almost-toddler. Milestones are helpful signposts along the way, but they are ranges, not deadlines. Here is what typically unfolds in each quarter of the first year , and how to think about it without anxiety.

0–3 months: settling in and waking up to the world

In the early weeks, movement is mostly reflexive , grasping a finger, startling at noise, rooting toward a feed. By around two to three months, many babies begin lifting their head during tummy time, bringing hands to their mouth, and moving arms and legs more smoothly.

Socially, this is the season of the first real smile, usually somewhere around six to eight weeks , a moment most parents never forget. Babies also start to calm at a familiar voice and study faces intently.

On the language front, expect coos, gurgles, and different cries for different needs. Talking back to those little sounds is one of the best things you can do.

4–6 months: rolling, reaching, and laughing

Motor skills take off in this stretch. Many babies roll over (front to back often comes first), push up on their arms during tummy time, sit with support, and reach for and grasp toys with growing accuracy.

Social development blooms too: expect belly laughs, squeals of delight, and clear recognition of familiar people. Babies this age often love simple games and studying their own hands.

Babbling begins in earnest , strings of sounds like "ba" and "ga" , and babies start responding to their own name and to changes in your tone of voice.

7–9 months: sitting, scooting, and stranger awareness

Most babies learn to sit steadily without support during this window, and many begin moving , scooting, rolling with purpose, or starting to crawl. Crawling styles vary widely, and some perfectly healthy babies skip crawling altogether.

This is also when separation anxiety and wariness of strangers commonly appear. It can feel like a step backward, but it is actually a sign of healthy attachment , your baby now clearly knows who their special people are.

Language-wise, babbling gets more varied and conversational, and babies begin to understand simple words like "no" and "bye-bye," often responding with gestures.

10–12 months: cruising toward toddlerhood

In the last quarter of the first year, many babies pull to stand, cruise along furniture, and stand alone briefly. Some take their first independent steps around their first birthday , though anywhere from about 9 to 18 months is a normal range for walking.

Fine motor skills sharpen too: the pincer grasp (thumb and forefinger) lets babies pick up small pieces of food, and they love dropping, banging, and putting objects in and out of containers.

First words often arrive around now , "mama," "dada," or a favorite object , along with waving, pointing, and following simple requests. Pointing is a big one: it shows your baby wants to share the world with you.

Every baby has their own pace

Milestone charts describe averages, and healthy babies land all over the range. Premature babies are usually tracked by their adjusted age, and it is common for a baby to surge in one area (say, motor skills) while another (like babbling) waits its turn.

Comparing your baby to a cousin, a neighbor, or a highlight reel on social media is a fast route to unnecessary worry. What matters most is steady progress over time, not the exact date any single skill appears.

When to mention delays to your doctor

Bring up anything that worries you at routine check-ups , that is exactly what they are for, and no concern is too small. It is especially worth mentioning if a baby loses skills they once had, does not respond to sounds or make eye contact, has very stiff or very floppy muscles, or is far outside typical ranges for several skills at once.

Early conversations lead to early support, and early support makes a real difference. Most of the time a doctor will offer reassurance; when extra help is needed, starting sooner is always better.

Önemli noktalar

  • Milestones are ranges, not deadlines , healthy babies vary widely.
  • Expect social smiles by 2–3 months, rolling and babbling by 4–6, sitting by 7–9, and cruising or first steps by 10–12.
  • Separation anxiety around 7–9 months is a sign of healthy attachment.
  • Track progress over time rather than comparing to other babies.
  • Mention lost skills, no response to sound, or multiple delays to your doctor early.

Sık sorulan sorular

My baby is not crawling , should I worry?

Probably not. Crawling styles vary enormously, and some healthy babies scoot, roll, or skip crawling entirely and go straight to standing. If your baby is progressing in other motor skills, mention it at a check-up for reassurance.

When do most babies take their first steps?

Around the first birthday on average, but anywhere from roughly 9 to 18 months is considered normal. Cruising along furniture usually comes first.

How are milestones counted for premature babies?

Doctors usually use adjusted age , your baby’s age counted from the original due date rather than the birth date , typically until about age two. Ask your provider how they track your baby.
